text:
Vegas needed a shootout to finish a comeback that the play had been demanding for most of two periods. TOR scored three times in the first 8:37, Jack Roslovic's backhand on a 4% chance among them, and led 3-0 while being outplayed. From there the game turned. Mark Stone cut it to 3-1 late in the first, Brett Howden deflected one in early in the second, and Jack Eichel tied it 3-3 at 3:58 of the period.

The gap between what happened and what the scoreboard showed was wide. VGK finished with 4.99 expected goals to TOR's 2.60 and 43 shots on goal to 24, and in the second period alone the chances ran 2.12 to 0.56. The model gives VGK an 82% share of simulated replays. Sergei Bobrovsky kept TOR alive, saving 1.99 goals more than the shots he faced should have cost. He stopped 40 of 43, and VGK went 0 for 4 on the power play despite 1.43 expected goals there.

Overtime solved nothing, though William Nylander had a 29% look that Adin Hill stopped. In the shootout, Braeden Bowman and Kirill Marchenko scored in the first round, then six straight shooters were stopped. Trevor Connelly scored in the fifth round, and John Tavares was stopped to end it, giving VGK a 4-3 win. Eichel, with a goal, an assist and 3.3 on-ice expected goals for against 0.52 against, drove the comeback, and Connelly took first star.
